text:
ravi: Heads-up — noticed a new eviction pattern this morning on small-slot pools in us-west2. pods with nodeAffinity 'anchor=true' are sticking and causing bursty backfills, then tiny GPU slots get starved.
alex: Hmm, saw the alerts. Is this the same anchor label we rolled out with the rack-reserve change?
kristin: yes — the rack-reserve PR added anchor=true to a handful of system-critical workloads so they don't move during AZ maintenance. thought that would be fine.
ravi: The problem is those anchors are heavy on tiny-slot nodes (1xA10g equivalently) and we have a new binpack heuristic that prefers filling tiny slots before large ones. When anchors land on a handful of tiny nodes, the scheduler refuses to pack medium pods onto those nodes and leaves scattered free GPU fraction that can't be used.
alex: Can you paste a couple of pod descriptions/logs? also which scheduler version?
ravi: here's a snippet from the binder logs:```Pod bind failed: no matching fit: node "gpu-tiny-7" has 0.2 free GPU but pod requests 0.25; affinity conflicts with anchor=true```
kristin: scheduler is v1.18.6-custom (the recent binpack tweak). We've seen edge cases in the sim but not at scale.
infra-bot: [alert] 4339000150 - node gpu-tiny-7 eviction cascade: 8 pods evicted in 3m; fragmentation score +0.32
sam: Short-term mitigation: can we relax the anchor placement constraint to prefer racks but allow node eviction when binpack score drops below threshold?
alex: We could also change the binpack heuristic to prefer consolidating on larger-slot nodes first when fragmentation > 0.25. That would avoid creating tiny unusable remainders.
kristin: Agree. Quick fix I'm proposing: patch scheduler to add 'preferLargeFirst' path for GPU fractional slots, and remove strict anti-evict from anchors for system-pods with toleration window 15m.
ravi: That sounds reasonable. Any cost tradeoffs? moving anchors to larger nodes could temporarily increase tail latency if they land on busier hosts.
sam: Cost: slightly higher peak used capacity but fewer forced evictions => less re-scheduling churn, so net lower vCPU/GPU-hours wasted.
alex: Okay, plan: patch scheduler in canary (us-west2 small-pools) then monitor fragmentation, eviction rate, and tail latency. Kristin can you open the canary PR? Ravi run a short simulation on current pod mix and post numbers here.
kristin: On it. I'll target a 30-min canary rollout and add a rollback job if eviction rate spikes > 50% of baseline.
ravi: Quick sim numbers: consolidation-first reduces unusable GPU fraction from 18% -> 5% in 10k-pod trace, estimated 12% fewer evictions. Posting full sim in #eng-platform later.
infra-bot: [deploy] canary patch scheduled 4339000168 -> eng-platform-us-west2-small (auto-rollback enabled)
alex: Nice. After canary, if metrics look good, we should also update the placement docs so teams know anchors aren't guaranteed immovable anymore.
kristin: Will update docs + notify ops.
sam: Thanks team — appreciate the quick loop. :thumbsup:
